Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In these two appeals, the appellant-owner- cum- driver of the goods auto is challenging the judgment and award dated 01.01.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.464/2013 and M.V.C.No.610/2013 by the learned Additional Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, Court of Small Causes and MACT,
Mysuru, ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the ranks of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, on 18.11.2012 at about 12 noon, the petitioners were riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA.09-EQ-6261, they were hit by the goods auto bearing No. KA.45-M-4277 for which the appellant is the owner- cum- driver.

Due to which, the petitioners fell NC:
2024:KHC:37483 down and sustained injuries.
After taking treatment at various hospitals at Mysore, they have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claims were opposed by the respondents.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment allowed the claim petitions of the petitioners by awarding compensation of Rs.1,45,500/-
to the petitioner in MVC No.464/2013 and Rs.2,16,500/- to the petitioner in MVC No.610/2013 by directing the owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a., and exonerated the insurance company from its liability.
Aggrieved by the same, the appellant-owner- cum- driver of the goods auto is before this Court in these appeals.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri Nagesh M., learned counsel for the appellant-owner-cum-driver of goods auto and Sri K.Nagarajaih, learned counsel for the Insurance Company in both these appeals.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant/owner-cum-driver of goods auto that, as on the NC: 2024:KHC:37483 date of accident, he was holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive the light motor vehicle, non- transport car, light motor vehicle three wheeler non- transport vehicle.
The said driving licence is effective from 7.3.2012, whereas, the accident took place on 18.11.2012.

Relies is placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited 1 to buttress that the driving licence held by the driver is sufficient to drive goods auto and the insurance company cannot avoid its liability and sought for direction to the insurance company to indemnify his liability.

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the material on record.
8. The accident is not in dispute.
The petitioners as well as the insurance company are not challenging the quantum of compensation.
The only point is regarding the liability fastened against the appellant/owner- cum- driver of the goods auto.
The officer of the insurance company is testified as RW1, copy of the insurance policy and driving licence extract are at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

On perusal of the driving licence extract, it is pertinent to note that the driver of the goods auto was holding driving licence to driver light motor vehicle, non transport car and also light 2006 SCC Online Karnataka 31 NC: 2024:KHC:37483
motor vehicle
3 wheeler
non transport
. The said driving licence was effective from 7.3.2012 onwards, whereas, the accident took place on 18.11.2012.
It goes to show that the driver of the goods auto was holding the said driving licence to drive the said category of vehicle.

9. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan's (refereed supra) held that the driving licence held by a person to drive the light motor vehicle is sufficient to drive all category of light motor vehicles.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Apex Court at para 60, 60.1 to 60.4 held as follows:
"60.

Thus, we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
60.1. "Light motor vehicle" as defined in Section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in Section 2(21) read with Sections 2(15) and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act 54 of 1994.

60.2. A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg would be a light motor vehicle and NC: 2024:KHC:37483 also motor car or tractor or a roadroller, "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.

A licence issued under Section 10(2)(d)
continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54 of 1994 and 28- Byregowda vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191113418/

sentences.text: 60.3. The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act 54 of 1994 w.e.f. 14-11-1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of Section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(e), "medium passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(f), "heavy goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(h) with expression "transport vehicle" as substituted in Section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of Section 10(2)(d) and Section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle"
is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle"
continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
10. In the light of the above law being laid down, driving licence held by driver is sufficient to drive the goods auto in question, which being a light motor vehicle.
In view of the change in circumstances, the insurance company has to indemnify the liability on the part of the insured.
The judgment of the co-ordinate Bench of this court regarding non application of pay and recover does not arise in this case as the entire liability is going against the insurance company.
